newsitem.title: CANADA: Inco union says rejects latest Sudbury offer.
newsitem.headline: Inco union says rejects latest Sudbury offer.

text.p: The union representing 4,700 Inco Ltd workers in Ontario said on Wednesday that it rejected the nickel miner's latest contract offer.
Negotiators for the United Steelworkers of America and Inco are trying to hammer out a new agreement before the current contract expires at midnight on Saturday, May 31.
"There was an offer this afternoon," Gary Patterson, vice-president of Steelworkers' local 6500, said in a telephone interview.
"It's certainly not anything close to resolving the differences that we have," he said, adding that the offer was quickly rejected by union negotiators.
Patterson said both sides are having trouble finding common ground on some non-monetary issues.
"Those issues for us unless they disappear will cause a strike regardless of what the monetary offer is," he said.
Earlier today, Inco spokesman Jerry Rogers said the company was optimistic that a deal could be reached.
"We're meeting continuously and we remain optimistic," Rogers said in a telephone interview.
On Monday, the Steelworkers requested the assistance of a provincial mediator after talks reached an impasse over the weekend.
Workers at Inco's Ontario operations have voted 98 percent in favor of giving union leaders a mandate to strike if a tentative agreement cannot be reached by May 31.
The contract affects 4,700 workers at the nickel giant's mining, smelting and refinery operations in Sudbury and its refinery in Port Colborne.
